papers.title: SWE-Bench ProMax: Benchmarking Agents on Large-Scale Multilingual Code Refactoring

summary.tldr: SWE-Bench ProMax is a multilingual code refactoring benchmark of 170 expert-curated instances across seven languages designed to address flaws and low complexity in existing coding agent benchmarks.
key_points: Covers seven programming languages: Python, Java, TypeScript, Go, C, C++, and Rust.
Instances are curated from real commits with manually rewritten issue descriptions and reviewed test suites to eliminate flawed tests.
Tasks require large-scale refactoring, averaging 11.4 modified files and 261.6 lines of code per instance.
Frontier models evaluated under two agent scaffolds achieved a peak resolve rate of 41.2%.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides an unsaturated, high-quality evaluation target that tests AI agents on complex, cross-file software refactoring without the noisy test suites of earlier benchmarks.

papers.title: Macaron-V1: Towards Open Continual Learning with Self-Improvement and Mixture-of-LoRA

summary.tldr: Macaron-V1 is an open agent-model family that uses recursive self-improvement and a Mixture-of-LoRA architecture to enable post-deployment continual learning.
key_points: Uses Mixture-of-LoRA (MoL) architecture to select one dynamic specialist LoRA adapter per user turn while keeping the base model frozen.
Features Macaron-V1-Venti (744B GLM-5.2 base) and Macaron-V1-Tall (50B Qwen3.6 base) equipped with four LoRAs for chat, agent, coding, and GenUI.
Includes algorithmic components like the UI4A component-native GenUI harness, stateful action substrates, versioned HCP contracts, and the MindForge agentic RL framework.
Supported by MinT post-training infrastructure, LongStraw long-context RL, and stability techniques designed for sparse MoE and DSA base models.
summary.why_it_matters: It offers an open-source co-designed infrastructure that allows deployed models to continuously adapt and specialize without retraining the underlying base weights.

papers.title: Motif 3: Technical Report

summary.tldr: Motif 3 is a 314B parameter decoder-only MoE model utilizing Grouped Differential Latent Attention, activating 13.2B parameters across 384 routed experts to improve efficiency, stability, and broad domain performance.
key_points: Architecture features 314B total and 13.2B active parameters per token, routing 8 of 384 experts per layer using Grouped Differential Latent Attention (GDLA) and Expert Specific PolyNorm activations.
Pretrained on ~12.5 trillion tokens up to 256K context length using selective MXFP8 mixed precision, fused kernels, and window-aware context parallelism.
Post-training uses Multi-teacher On-Policy Distillation to combine six RL-trained specialist teachers and one SFT software-engineering teacher into a single unified model.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates how combining fine-grained MoE sparsity, architectural stabilization, and multi-teacher distillation can yield top-tier performance across reasoning, coding, and long-context tasks with reduced active compute per token.

papers.title: Agent Memory Distillation: Empowering Small LLM Agents with Hierarchical Teacher Memory

summary.tldr: Agent Memory Distillation (AMD) is a training-free framework that transfers structured, hierarchical teacher memory (Workflow, Subtask, and Function) from large LLMs to small 4B-8B student agents to boost tool-use performance.
key_points: AMD builds three memory types from teacher trajectories: Workflow (task strategies), Subtask (intermediate behaviors), and Function (tool conventions and pitfalls).
Workflow and Subtask memories are injected proactively at task initialization, whereas Function memory is retrieved reactively after tool-calling errors.
Evaluated with a GPT-5-mini teacher, AMD improved 4B-8B student model accuracy by 27.2%p on AppWorld, 11.2%p on BFCL V3, and 3.4%p on ToolSandbox.
Subtask memory provides the largest individual performance gains, with 4B-parameter models benefiting more than 8B-parameter models.
summary.why_it_matters: AMD enables small language models (4B-8B parameters) to achieve high-tier tool-use capabilities without requiring expensive model retraining or fine-tuning.

papers.title: Sci-VBench: Evaluating Knowledge- and Reasoning-Intensive Video Generation in Science Domains

summary.tldr: Sci-VBench is a new benchmark featuring 1,253 expert-annotated examples across 60 subjects to evaluate scientific reasoning and knowledge-grounded synthesis in video generation models.
key_points: Covers four core disciplines: Natural Science, Healthcare, Humanities & Social Sciences, and Engineering.
Establishes a rubric-based evaluation protocol where non-expert human evaluators and MLLM-as-Judge systems align closely with expert judgments.
Evaluation of 16 frontier models reveals narrow gaps in visual realism, but wide disparity between proprietary and open-source models in Prompt Grounding and Scientific and Causal Correctness.
summary.why_it_matters: The benchmark demonstrates that high perceptual quality in AI-generated video does not guarantee accurate modeling of real-world scientific and causal dynamics.

papers.title: Ouroboros: A Self-Developing Frontier Coding Agent with Reviewed Core Evolution

summary.tldr: Ouroboros is a self-developing coding agent that recursively evolves its tools, prompts, context assembly, and core implementation through governed, reviewed commits.
key_points: Operates via two modes: recursive free evolution (self-scheduled improvement cycles) and experience-driven core evolution (refining code based on bugs and interactions exposed during ordinary work).
Achieves benchmark state-of-the-art results using Opus 5: 86.74% on Terminal-Bench 2.1, 90.69% on OSWorld-Verified, and a 0.2301 normalized reward on CL-Bench across a five-rollout campaign.
Tested via 'Hope', a 161-day live deployment across seven human communication surfaces where the agent autonomously decides which human-surfaced proposals and faults to implement.
Enforces strict guardrail authority to maintain operational safety as the agent self-rewrites code and selects new model APIs under social and evolutionary pressure.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that software agents can continuously self-improve their own codebase and performance on complex tasks without losing operational control or safety.

papers.title: DCAS: Decoupling CLI Agent Scaffolding to Internalize Planning across Scaffolds

summary.tldr: DCAS is an interception layer that decouples CLI agent scaffolding from backend models to train LLMs on planning-aware trajectories, mitigating fine-tuning-induced performance degradation across different evaluation scaffolds.
key_points: Trajectory datasets collected under a single scaffold (e.g., OpenHands) cause fine-tuned open models to suffer significant performance drops when deployed on non-training scaffolds.
DCAS functions as a backend-substitution interception layer that routes API traffic between any CLI scaffold and backend model without modifying scaffold source code.
DCAS enables planning-aware trajectory collection by separating planning into explicit (pre-execution artifacts) and implicit (structural execution conventions) forms.
Fine-tuning on a small set of DCAS-collected trajectories under one scaffold yields consistent performance gains across non-training scaffolds.
summary.why_it_matters: Decoupling planning from scaffold-specific artifacts allows models to internalize planning as a native capability, ensuring robust agent performance across diverse CLI environments.

papers.title: SPOT: Sparse Probing and Outcome Calibration for On-Policy Distillation

summary.tldr: SPOT improves on-policy distillation by using an acquisition-exploration-exploitation framework that sparsely probes teacher-proposed top-k candidates and calibrates distillation targets using verifier-scored student continuations.
key_points: Address limitations of standard reverse-KL training and local teacher probability estimates during on-policy distillation.
Acquisition phase allocates a probing budget based on normalized teacher entropy, top-k captured probability mass, and student-teacher mismatch.
Exploration phase evaluates teacher candidates via verifier-scored student continuations.
Exploitation phase constructs a closed-form, KL-regularized distillation target anchored to the teacher distribution but favoring higher-reward outcomes.
summary.why_it_matters: SPOT enhances student model reasoning performance by ensuring distillation targets reflect downstream solution success rather than just local teacher token probabilities.

papers.title: Small Foundation Models of Human Cognition and Behaviour

summary.tldr: Fourteen language models (135M to 14B parameters) fine-tuned on the 10.7M-trial Psych-101 dataset show that 0.6B-1B parameter models match 70B baselines in-distribution, though larger models scale significantly better out-of-distribution.
key_points: Evaluated 14 models across four architecture families using 10.7 million trial-level choices from 160 experiments in the Psych-101 dataset.
Models between 0.6B and 1B parameters match the performance of a 70B parameter baseline on held-out participants for in-distribution tasks.
Out-of-distribution performance displays a steep scaling gradient, favoring larger models when generalizing to novel task structures.
A four-channel prompt-stripping diagnostic showed that masking stimuli and feedback content destroyed 75.7% of learned information, dropping performance below chance.
Trial-order permutation tests showed models are invariant on independent-trial tasks, but sensitive when trial sequence depends on prior responses.
summary.why_it_matters: Small cognitively fine-tuned models can efficiently serve as noise ceiling estimators for human psychological experiments without requiring massive 70B-parameter models for in-distribution tasks.

papers.title: OasisKV: Scaling In-Decode KV Cache Beyond HBM with Lookahead Sparse Prefetching

summary.tldr: OasisKV decouples full KV-cache storage from HBM by using speculative decoding's lookahead tokens to predict and prefetch sparse, high-importance KV blocks from host/remote memory into HBM ahead of decode steps.
key_points: Uses speculative decoding lookahead tokens and an attention background pipeline to accurately predict and prefetch critical KV blocks from host or remote memory tiers into HBM.
Maintains accuracy within 0.7 points of full attention using a 2,048-token KV budget.
Achieves 1.69x throughput gains over dense vLLM on reasoning tasks and up to 2.1x on multi-GPU long-context serving.
Reduces per-request KV admission requirements by 6.5-9.7x and decode-node host memory overhead by 2.2-2.6x under prefill-decode disaggregation.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables memory-constrained inference systems to process significantly larger batch sizes and long-context workloads with up to double the throughput without losing generation accuracy.

papers.title: Relevant but Incomplete: Referential Dangling as a Paradigm-Level Failure Mode in Hard Prompt Compression

summary.tldr: Independent scoring in hard prompt compression causes referential dangling, where retained answer text loses the required entity context, degrading downstream model accuracy by up to 34 percentage points.
key_points: Referential dangling occurs when independent compression algorithms select answer-bearing text while dropping the contextual entity definition needed to interpret it.
At a 0.30 compression ratio, the Beaver compressor creates incomplete answer paths in 34-54% of bridge examples, while six tested compressors exhibit dangling rates up to 60% on HotpotQA.

Reinserting missing supporting paragraphs improves Qwen3-8B accuracy by 29-34 percentage points, while advanced models like GPT-5.5 still show an 8.8-point accuracy drop on compressed MuSiQue contexts.
An automated classifier trained to reinsert missing referential sentences yields a 4.7-point accuracy gain on HotpotQA while shifting the compression ratio minimally from 0.30 to 0.31.
summary.why_it_matters: Hard prompt compression algorithms must be redesigned to ensure referential completeness alongside relevance, as even frontier language models cannot recover lost contextual dependencies.

papers.title: Multi-Agent Forensic Reasoning for Generalizable Deepfake Video Detection

summary.tldr: A new framework, FaceVid-Forensics-100K dataset, and multi-agent system improve deepfake video detection by analyzing four distinct forensic perspectives using open-source MLLMs.
key_points: FaceVid-Forensics-100K dataset contains 100,000 videos spanning 33 synthesis methods, including Seedance 2.0, with MLLM-synthesized textual annotations and forensic explanations.
The multi-agent framework deploys four specialized domain-expert agents to evaluate texture, lighting, motion, and physics cues independently.
A dedicated judge agent resolves conflicts among expert reports to output a final verdict and explanation.
Composed of small open-source MLLMs, the framework ranks first across all benchmark metrics, outperforming closed-source models like GPT and Gemini on out-of-domain test sets.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach provides generalizable deepfake detection and interpretable forensic reasoning without relying on large closed-source multimodal language models.

papers.title: Evo-Bench: Can Language Models Improve Agent Harness?

summary.tldr: Evo-Bench is the first benchmark designed to evaluate LLMs' intrinsic capacity to autonomously evolve their own operating harnesses across Search, Office, and General agent domains.
key_points: Evo-Bench uses a harness-guided construction framework featuring auxiliary-task evolution and sensitivity-aware stratified splitting to isolate harness capabilities from base model strength.
Evaluations across nine models showed top LLMs achieving up to 16.6 point absolute gains, approaching human-engineered baselines.
Autonomous harness evolution outperformed artificial harnesses in General tasks and excelled in Search tasks, but underperformed in Office tasks requiring specific workflows.
Synthesized harnesses exhibited temporal anomalies like early saturation, yet functioned as highly transferable reasoning structures that boosted diverse policy models.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides a standardized methodology to evaluate whether LLMs can self-optimize their execution frameworks, opening pathways for transferable, self-improving AI agent architectures.

papers.title: Evidence-RL: Towards Evidence-intensive Visual Reasoning

summary.tldr: Counterfactual Evidence Disentanglement (CED) improves Vision-Language Model grounding by auditing whether model responses causally depend on specific visual evidence regions during Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) training.
key_points: CED neutralizes object-centric Evidence Regions during training and measures response support drop against non-evidence control regions to detect visual shortcuts.
The counterfactual evidence signal is integrated into GRPO to reward correct answers that causally rely on the grounded evidence path.
The framework uses weak object-level proposals and requires zero question-specific evidence annotations or inference-time compute overhead.
Evaluations across four VLM backbones and nine benchmarks show CED outperforms prior reinforcement learning post-training methods.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables Vision-Language Models to reduce hallucinations and dataset shortcuts by forcing causal reliance on visual context without incurring additional inference costs or requiring manual evidence annotations.

papers.title: Scaling Inherently Interpretable Language Models

summary.tldr: Researchers introduced Steerling-8B, demonstrating that incorporating interpretability constraints directly into training pipelines allows interpretability to scale alongside language modeling capability without sacrificing performance.
key_points: Interpretability was integrated directly into the training pipeline and optimized alongside the language modeling objective across autoregressive and diffusion models.
Model scale improved representation disentanglement and alignment with human-understandable concepts across three orders of magnitude of compute.
Steerling-8B, an 8-billion parameter diffusion language model with a causal attention mask, attributes token outputs to specific input tokens, concepts, and training data.
The architecture enables closed-loop interventions, allowing output diagnosis, training data retrieval, and real-time concept steering corrections without retraining.
Steerling-8B achieves performance competitive with open peer models trained on 2x to 16x more compute.
summary.why_it_matters: It proves that models can be built inherently interpretable and steerable at scale without paying a performance penalty or requiring expensive compute-heavy post-hoc analysis.

papers.title: Mismatch Matters: On-Policy Distillation Beyond Token Agreement

summary.tldr: TIDE improves on-policy distillation by addressing teacher-student mismatch via bounded Hellinger shaping for student-excess tokens and analytic teacher top-K injection for student-deficit tokens.
key_points: Identifies degenerate agreement in on-policy distillation, where students use repetitive loops to achieve high token agreement while outputting globally flawed responses.

Categorizes token mismatches into student-excess tokens (generated by student, near-zero probability by teacher) which destabilize updates, and student-deficit tokens (preferred by teacher, rarely sampled by student) which block reasoning transfer.
Introduces TIDE, which uses bounded Hellinger shaping to suppress severe excess tokens and analytic top-K injection to restore deficit probability mass without needing deficit tokens to be sampled.

Demonstrates that TIDE outperforms standard OPD and baselines on mathematical benchmarks using Qwen3 teacher-student pairs, raising Avg@8 from 6.9% to 20.3% under strong mismatch while reducing average response length by 3.6x.
summary.why_it_matters: TIDE stabilizes on-policy distillation under severe model mismatches, preventing degenerate generation loops and reducing formatting failures while shortening response lengths.

papers.title: Distill Skills into Weights, Not Prompts: Abstract Skills as Privileged Signals for On-Policy Self-Distillation

summary.tldr: SKALD uses on-policy self-distillation to transfer knowledge from a teacher model conditioned on abstract skills into a question-only student model, overcoming zero-variance reward groups in reinforcement learning.
key_points: Addresses the issue where 63.0-68.0% of rollout groups in RL with verifiable rewards yield no group-relative signal due to uniform correctness or failure.
Uses a Qwen3-Base teacher model conditioned on an abstract, explicit-answer-filtered skill card to distill knowledge into a question-only student model trained on its own prefixes.

Stabilizes context-induced distribution mismatch using an annealed exponentially tilted objective that downweights teacher tokens with very low student likelihood, converging to forward-KL student gradient as tilt vanishes.
Employs an empirical gate that activates distillation only when verified rollouts indicate a positive teacher advantage.
Improves avg@8 over GRPO across five held-out math benchmarks by +2.46, +4.85, and +12.01 on 0.6B, 1.7B, and 4B models, with zero-variance-only distillation recovering 84.7% of the gain at 1.7B.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables language models to internalize abstract reasoning skills directly into their weights, offering dense learning signals even when standard RL reward signals stall.

papers.title: Parameter Exploration for RLVR via Variational Learning

summary.tldr: Researchers introduced Perturbed Parameter Policy Optimization (3PO), a parameter-space exploration framework for LLM reinforcement learning that samples diverse policy parameters to improve exploration beyond traditional action-space methods.
key_points: Standard action-space exploration techniques like temperature scaling cannot reorder tokens and only adjust output distribution variance, leading to stalled training or divergence.
3PO executes parameter-space exploration by sampling different policies from a posterior to generate rollouts, incorporating distinct sampling strategies and rollout grouping for reward estimation.
Experiments using OLMo-3-1025-7B and Qwen2.5-Math-7B on math reasoning and code generation tasks demonstrated consistent performance improvements over GRPO at near-identical FLOP costs.
Using multiple parameter samples reduced zero-advantage groups and malformed rollouts during training compared to GRPO and action-space baselines.
summary.why_it_matters: Parameter-space exploration provides a FLOP-efficient alternative to action-space methods, improving LLM reinforcement learning stability and task performance without additional computational overhead.

papers.title: SR-OPSD: Self-Referenced On-Policy Self-Distillation

summary.tldr: SR-OPSD introduces a self-referenced on-policy self-distillation framework that stabilizes optimization by placing distillation targets via geometric interpolation and controlling projection geometry using Rényi divergence.
key_points: Addresses instability and distributional concentration caused by co-evolving self-teacher policies and student distributions in standard OPSD.
Derives a token-level variational characterization that identifies distillation targets as geometric interpolations between a self-teacher policy and a reference policy.
Employs the Rényi divergence family to separate target placement (controlled by interpolation coefficients) from projection geometry and density ratio sensitivity (controlled by Rényi order).
summary.why_it_matters: It improves optimization stability and performance across scientific, mathematical, and code generation tasks when tuning large language models with dense token-level feedback.

papers.title: Matryoshka Language Model Suites

summary.tldr: A novel Matryoshka training framework stacks language sub-models into a single nested architecture, enabling end-to-end joint training, in-flight distillation, and parameter-efficient speculative decoding.
key_points: Combines 500M, 1.5B, and 3B sub-models into a single nested architecture trained end-to-end.
Reduces total training compute by 36% while matching independently trained baseline models in benchmark performance, validation, and out-of-domain perplexity.
Enables low-cost distillation from the largest to smaller sub-models at every training step.
Increases speculative decoding throughput by 14-26% by utilizing the nested small sub-model as the draft model for the larger verifier.
summary.why_it_matters: This architecture significantly cuts pre-training compute costs and enhances inference throughput without sacrificing model performance across size variants.

papers.title: MixFormer: Linear Transformer with Mixture of Memory Experts

summary.tldr: MixFormer is a linear Transformer that combines a Mixture-of-Memory-Experts mechanism with Time-Aware Linear Attention to improve memory capacity and long-context sequence modeling.
key_points: Integrates a Mixture-of-Memory-Experts (MoE) architecture that uses multiple collaborating experts to maintain differentiated memory states.
Introduces Time-Aware Linear Attention (TALA) using learnable exponential decay functions and positional biases for dynamic memory updates.
Mitigates memory dilution and information loss present in standard State Space Models (SSMs) during ultra-long sequence processing.
Demonstrates performance improvements in long-sequence text and image generation tasks.
summary.why_it_matters: By overcoming the memory capacity and input adaptivity limitations of standard SSMs, MixFormer offers a more computationally efficient backbone for long-context web infrastructure and generative tasks.

papers.title: WDL-OPD: Weak-Driven On-Policy Distillation via Mixture-Constrained Co-Training

summary.tldr: WDL-OPD stabilizes on-policy distillation by co-training an anchor policy and an auxiliary policy using a mixture-constrained reverse KL loss against a frozen teacher.
key_points: Uses an anchor policy for rollouts and an auxiliary policy for state evaluation, matching their token distribution geometric mixture to a frozen teacher via reverse KL.
Freezing the auxiliary policy recovers an anchor-plus-contrast proxy target related to OPD2 and W2S-OPD, while joint training adds dynamic branch-level degrees of freedom.
Evaluated on Qwen3 1.7B and 4B models, raising MATH500 accuracy to 0.585 (1.7B) and 0.685 (4B), outperforming four scale-domain baselines.
Mitigates entropy growth and trajectory degradation seen in seven single-policy OPD configurations during code generation, achieving dev scores of 0.637 and 0.375.
summary.why_it_matters: Co-training two policies via a geometric mixture offers a targeted mechanism to prevent feedback loop instabilities and performance degradation in on-policy LLM distillation.

papers.title: Depth-adaptive Inference of Looped Language Models via Continuous Depth Batching

summary.tldr: Continuous depth batching (CDB) enables efficient depth-adaptive inference for looped LMs by scheduling at the loop-iteration level while handling non-looped boundary stages via separate priority queues.
key_points: Depth-adaptive inference breaks standard token-level batching because tokens within the same batch exit at different iteration counts.
CDB manages non-looped boundary stages (embeddings and LM heads) and loop steps using separate priority queues.
Exit decisions are evaluated one step ahead, and all scheduling overhead is overlapped with GPU computation.
Evaluated on Ouro 1.4B and Huginn 3.5B, CDB achieves up to 99% of theoretical adaptive-depth speedups.
summary.why_it_matters: CDB resolves batching inefficiencies in looped language models, enabling 1.5-1.9x higher offline throughput and up to 90% lower latency under dynamic serving loads.

papers.title: A Mechanistic Diagnostic of Rank Collapse in Post-Norm Decoder Transformers

summary.tldr: A two-stage analysis reveals that Post-Norm Transformer rank collapse stems from causal attention amplifying forward token similarity, which causes pre-norm residual norm growth that geometrically contracts backward gradients in RMSNorm layers.
key_points: Initialization-time similarity growth is driven primarily by causal attention acting as a prefix-averaging operator, with SwiGLU providing only a minor damping effect.
Entering a high-similarity regime increases pre-normalization residual norms, making the backward factor of RMSNorm contractive and forcing geometric decay of gradients to earlier layers.
Collapsed Post-Norm networks decay to predicting token frequency distributions, where gradients vanish and training reaches a high loss floor.
Empirical evaluations on 48-layer decoder-only Transformers trained on C4 confirm the predicted similarity growth, gradient contraction, and frequency loss convergence.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding the distinct forward amplification and backward gradient contraction mechanisms in Post-Norm architectures provides a clear diagnostic for why training dynamics fail to recover from rank collapse.

papers.title: Reducing Pretraining-Generation Mismatch in Diffusion Language Models

summary.tldr: Prefix-Conditioned Diffusion (PCD) reduces pretraining-generation mismatch in diffusion language models by combining autoregressive prefix supervision with no-shift suffix denoising without changing the inference mode.
key_points: Identifies that native dLLM pretraining corrupts prompt and continuation tokens simultaneously, creating a mismatch with prompt-conditioned generation at evaluation time.
PCD alters the attention mask, corruption mask, and label construction during continued pretraining to autoregressively supervise the clean prefix while applying diffusion solely to the suffix.
Separates intra-sample prefix conditioning from inter-sample objective mixing to isolate the local alignment signal.
Yields a 4.2% relative gain (+2.56 points) on the LLaDA2-Mini six-benchmark average and a 14.2% relative gain (+4.86 points) in Qwen-1.7B mechanism evaluations over native dLLM baselines.
summary.why_it_matters: PCD narrows the performance gap between diffusion and autoregressive language models on continuation tasks without needing verifiers, extra decoders, or changes to inference.

security.title: Stealing Reasoning Traces from Proprietary LLM APIs

summary.tldr: Researchers exposed a vulnerability in LLM providers where encrypted client-side reasoning traces are interchangeable across sessions, allowing adversaries to decrypt them using weaker models.
key_points: Encrypted chain-of-thought blocks are fully compatible across different sessions, users, and models within Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google ecosystems.
Injecting a high-capability model's encrypted trace into a weaker, less-safeguarded model forces the weaker model to output the reasoning verbatim in plaintext.
Analysis of 315,320 public reasoning blocks yielded 367 PII artifacts and 182 credentials leaked via developer session logs.
The vulnerability enables four attack vectors: anti-distillation circumvention, private data extraction, leakage of hazardous hidden reasoning, and invisible prompt injection.
summary.why_it_matters: This architectural flaw allows attackers to steal proprietary IP, extract sensitive user credentials, and bypass safety guardrails without directly jailbreaking primary models.

security.title: ColluSkill: Adversarial Cross-Skill Composition for Evading Agent Skill Scanners

summary.tldr: ColluSkill is a framework that evades LLM agent skill scanners by splitting malicious payloads across interdependent skills, alongside ChainGuard, a defensive scanner that detects workflow-level risks.
key_points: Existing skill scanners inspect skills individually, creating a blind spot for risks that emerge only through cross-skill composition.
ColluSkill decomposes malicious intents into sub-payloads spread across separate skills using LLM-based chain planning and scanner-feedback refinement.
ColluSkill achieved a 96.0% average attack success rate against six existing skill scanners.

ChainGuard evaluates candidate skills against installed skills by analyzing dependencies, artifact flows, and capability compositions, reducing ColluSkill's success rate to 22.5% with a 99.5% benign pass rate.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that single-skill security checks are insufficient for LLM agents, necessitating workflow-level analysis to prevent multi-skill collusion.

security.title: Activation Probes Surface Code-Security Signals that the Model's Output Misses

summary.tldr: Linear probes trained on open-weight model activations detect software vulnerabilities that the same model fails to surface through direct text prompting or chain-of-thought reasoning.
key_points: A single linear probe was trained per model on paired vulnerable-and-fixed Python functions and evaluated on unseen weakness types from real disclosed vulnerabilities.
Across five open-weight models, the probe identified vulnerable functions over their fixes in 61-67% of single-function cases, significantly outperforming chance.
Probing internal activations outperformed prompted YES/NO logit win-rates across all tested prompt variations.
Written model verdicts, including those using chain-of-thought, frequently returned identical answers for both vulnerable and fixed functions, failing to distinguish between them.
summary.why_it_matters: Open-weight models can act as internal-activation security reviewers for code generated by closed-weight AI agents, extracting safety signals that surface-level text outputs omit.

security.title: Measuring the Wrong Thing: Internal Harmfulness Scores Anti-Rank Successful Jailbreaks

summary.tldr: A study reveals internal harmfulness scores anti-rank successful jailbreaks, rating effective wrapped attacks as safer than failed ones across multiple models, attack families, and judges.
key_points: Wrapping harmful prompts raised Llama harmful generation from 0.05 to 0.27 while harmful intent AUROC dropped from 0.936 to 0.803.
Among wrapped harmful prompts, the outcome AUROC fell to 0.220, placing successful jailbreaks below failed ones in internal safety score rankings.
Active Attention Probing was introduced to provide a fixed, content-independent measurement coordinate for attention-based safety evaluation.
The score reversal persisted across three target models, seven attack families, two judges, and occurred in rare token, passive, and detector-derived channels.
summary.why_it_matters: Filters relying on internal harmfulness scores waste their false-positive budgets on failed attacks while letting high-risk, successful jailbreaks pass undetected.

security.title: From Runnable to Verifiable: An Independent Reproducibility Study of LLM/Agent-Driven Vulnerability Validation Artifacts

summary.tldr: A pre-registered study of LLM-driven vulnerability validation artifacts reveals that only 56.7% are public, 61.1% run successfully after repairs, and internal verification oracles suffer from poor specificity (45%) and sensitivity (60%).
key_points: 58 out of 102 (56.9%) anchor benchmark cases contained an internal script CVE identifier that diverged from the declared directory CVE.
Only 10 of 18 (55.6%) sampled paper artifacts completed their workflow out-of-the-box (R0), rising to 11 of 18 (61.1%) after environment-only (R1) repairs.
Artifact-embedded oracles were unreliable: 20 of 30 patched-counterfactual audits produced signal on patched builds, and 7 of 19 matched negative controls triggered on benign inputs.
summary.why_it_matters: Vulnerability validation tools triggering on a vulnerable build cannot be trusted as evidence of a specific CVE reproduction without strict patched-counterfactual and negative-control testing.

security.title: Dual-Adversarial Safety Alignment: Cultivating Intrinsic Threat Comprehension in LRMs

summary.tldr: AdvSafe uses a dual-adversarial framework to train LRMs on 1K synthesized samples, teaching models intrinsic threat comprehension to improve jailbreak robustness without degrading reasoning utility.
key_points: Phase 1 (Adversarial Synthesis): An autonomous agent dynamically generates deceptive jailbreak prompts that adaptively breach a strong teacher model.
Phase 2 (Adversarial Extraction): The breached teacher executes a counter-attack by unmasking prompt camouflage, explaining the attack mechanism, and identifying mitigation steps.
Student models undergo safety alignment by fine-tuning on a compact 1K reasoning dataset containing these extracted unsafety explanations.
The approach improves out-of-distribution jailbreak robustness and maintains a superior robustness-utility trade-off compared to pattern-centric baselines.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables large reasoning models to generalize defenses against unseen attack patterns using minimal synthetic data while avoiding performance drops on benign reasoning tasks.

security.title: RangeFactory: Scalable Construction of Multi-Hop Cyber Ranges

summary.tldr: RangeFactory is an automated orchestration framework that constructs and validates multi-hop cyber ranges at scale by formulating range generation as a dependency resolution problem based on real attack trajectories.
key_points: Formulates range construction via dependency resolution: extracts dependency data from real attacks, resolves them with template-guided orchestration, and validates runtime dependencies via end-to-end execution.
Used to build RangeBench, which comprises 1,148 validated range instances across 287 unique attack chains.
Generates a corpus of 5,541 outcome-annotated multi-hop attack trajectories for process analysis and agent training.
Evaluation showed that 24.5-47.0% of agent runs compromising the entry vulnerability failed on subsequent steps, highlighting a sustained-compromise gap.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables scalable, automated benchmark creation and dataset generation to evaluate and train LLM agents on complex, multi-stage cyberattack chains.

security.title: STAIR: Effective Incident Response Using an End-to-End Agentic Planning Framework

summary.tldr: STAIR is an end-to-end agentic incident response framework that combines Graph-as-State tracking, stage-specialized LLM agents, and experience retrieval to adaptively resolve cyberattacks.
key_points: Maintains incident state using a Graph-as-State representation updated via an Execution Harness that runs actions and validates feedback.
Employs a Stage Router to route planning tasks to stage-specialized agents based on the current recovery objectives.
Utilizes historical experience retrieval to guide action selection and improve long-horizon planning stability.
Achieved a 0.94 normalized defense score across 100 Docker-based cyber ranges, outperforming the top baseline by 9.5%.
summary.why_it_matters: STAIR replaces static, brittle incident response playbooks with an adaptive, feedback-driven agent system that improves automated system recovery during complex cyberattacks.

security.title: ActBench: Self-Evolving Benchmark of Behavioral Safety in Cowork Agents

summary.tldr: ActBench is a self-evolving benchmark evaluating cowork agent behavioral safety from execution trajectories using adversarial task-reachable payloads optimized via reward-guided beam search.
key_points: Evaluates execution trajectories rather than final responses across 600 cases, 213 scenarios, 15 risk behaviors, 6 execution spaces, and 48 web-service APIs.
Adversarial cases pair benign tasks with payload injections while holding instructions, configurations, initial states, rating models, and trusted records constant.
Payload generation uses reward-guided beam search optimizing attack effectiveness and task utility, alongside reflection-based payload revision from failed checkpoints.
Employs a dual evidence verification mechanism using log evidence and LLM-based trajectory evidence to verify execution safety and utility.
Empirical evaluation of 15 LLMs and 6 agents across 24,000 trajectories yielded attack success rates of 10.1% to 94.4% across models and 73.7% to 94.4% across agent harnesses.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that current cowork agents remain highly vulnerable to behavioral safety risks like unauthorized API calls and data disclosure during task execution regardless of the underlying agent harness.

security.title: DiffSafeMerge: Mitigating Backdoor Inheritance in Diffusion Model Merging

summary.tldr: DiffSafeMerge (DSM) mitigates backdoor inheritance during diffusion checkpoint merging by using a clean dataset and attack-agnostic stress probes to attenuate suspicious model blocks under a denoising-loss budget.
key_points: Uses a small unlabeled clean reference set and fixed, attack-agnostic stress probes to evaluate and score individual source blocks.
Shrinks suspicious block contributions toward a trusted reference checkpoint and selects attenuation levels constrained by a clean denoising-loss budget.
Eliminated backdoor success in four high-risk merge cases (baseline ASR 48–100%) down to zero target matches across three seeds evaluated.
Achieved the lowest case-averaged FID among all evaluated defense methods that successfully reached zero worst-target ASR across two datasets.
summary.why_it_matters: DSM allows developers to safely merge public diffusion model checkpoints without risking backdoor vulnerability inheritance or sacrificing clean image generation quality.

security.title: Governing the KV Cache: Preventing Timing Side-Channel Leakage in Multi-Tenant LLM Inference

summary.tldr: KVGov introduces cryptographic per-principal salting and a water-filling audit scheduler to eliminate timing side-channel prompt-extraction attacks in shared multi-tenant LLM key-value caches without sacrificing efficiency.
key_points: Eliminates PROMPTPEEK, EarlyBird, and InputSnatch timing side-channel attacks by seeding the block-hash chain with a per-principal salt (sigma_p = HMAC_K(secret, principal_id)) to make cache keys cryptographically disjoint.
Injects the salt at the prompt divergence boundary rather than the chain root, retaining an estimated 93% of prefix-cache efficiency while blocking cross-principal leakage.
Includes ORIGAMI, a Stackelberg water-filling audit scheduler that decreases expected adversary utility by 12.6% under realistic tenant heterogeneity (Gini 0.63).
Empirically verifies the exploitable timing channel on production hardware, measuring cold/cached TTFT ratios of 0.22 on vLLM/NVIDIA A100 (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct) and 0.093 on llama.cpp/Apple Metal.
summary.why_it_matters: Multi-tenant LLM inference providers can secure shared prefix-caching architectures against full prompt reconstruction attacks with minimal loss in throughput.

security.title: Beyond Direct Identifiers: Probabilistic Privacy Risk Estimation for Privacy-Conscious LLM Query Delegation

summary.tldr: A probabilistic variant of Privacy-Conscious Delegation integrates LLM-driven k-anonymity estimation using the new PUPA-SD dataset to account for quasi-identifying self-disclosures beyond explicit PII.
key_points: Introduces the PUPA-SD dataset containing naturalistic user queries that feature PII-free self-disclosures and quasi-identifying traits.
Augments Privacy-Conscious Delegation (PCD) objectives with an LLM-driven probabilistic estimation of k-anonymity.
Optimizing the PAPILLON method on PUPA-SD improves unseen conversation quality across local models, achieving the best privacy-utility trade-off on Llama-3.2-3B.
Demonstrates that smaller local LLMs struggle to simultaneously optimize query quality and privacy metrics.
summary.why_it_matters: Using probabilistic k-anonymity as an auxiliary metric prevents user re-identification from combinations of quasi-identifiers when delegating queries to remote LLMs.

security.title: Joint Lyapunov Certificates for K-Agent Generative AI Governance: Stochastic Stability, Emergent Ensemble Risk, and Zero-Knowledge Governance Attestation

summary.tldr: A Joint Lyapunov Proof protocol provides zero-knowledge SNARK attestations to verify stochastic stability and prevent emergent ensemble drift in coupled multi-agent generative AI systems under Model Risk Management standards.
key_points: Demonstrates that individual per-agent Lyapunov stability is insufficient when $K$ self-adapting AI models interact via a meta-learning coupling matrix.
Derives a complete characterization of the infinitesimal generator for a joint quadratic Lyapunov function and calculates the exact critical coupling threshold for mean-square stability.
Proves a Noise-Floor Theorem to establish target bounds for zero-knowledge governance attestation.
Constructs a per-epoch Succinct Non-Interactive Argument of Knowledge (SNARK) enabling attestation on live model weights without disclosing proprietary parameter values.
Validates theoretical results using five numerical experiments on a multi-agent softmax system.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables institutions to cryptographically verify that interconnected AI models meet safety and stability regulations without forcing vendors to expose private model weights.

security.title: Telemetry and Concealment in Self-Adapting Generative AI: Logging Architecture, Adversarial Model Hiding, and the Limits of Detection

summary.tldr: This paper presents a dual-regime telemetry architecture for self-adapting generative AI, combining Merkle chains, continuous-time Ito telemetry, and KL divergence stopping times alongside a six-strategy attack taxonomy with countermeasures.
key_points: Combines discrete Merkle chains for weight updates and continuous-time Ito calculus generalizations to create a tamper-evident audit log.
Implements event-driven telemetry logging using KL divergence stopping times to maintain computational tractability during online weight updates.
Formalizes the Model Hiding Problem, identifying six distinct adversarial strategies used to conceal learning updates from auditors.
Pairs each of the six model-hiding attack strategies with a formal countermeasure to enforce continuous monitoring.
Demonstrates that continuous telemetry reduces reliance on point-in-time validation without completely eliminating periodic invasive audits.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides a concrete logging and security framework to help continuously updating generative models meet traditional Model Risk Management requirements.

security.title: Repeated-Game Security for Restaking-Based Verifiable Inference

summary.tldr: Researchers revealed that standard one-round slashing in restaking-based LLM inference fails under repeated games, proposing a history-dependent, reputation-weighted mechanism that restores subgame-perfect incentive compatibility.
key_points: Proportional slashing creates a repeated-game gap where detected deviations lower future penalty exposure while dishonest cost savings accumulate across queries.
Surveyed restaking protocols pass one-round security checks but allow profitable repeated-game deviations (1.5%–8% profit fractions) at discount factors between 0.92 and 0.98.

The proposed defense integrates history-dependent challenges, reputation-weighted slashing, and stake vesting to secure infinite-horizon subgame-perfect incentives without per-query cryptographic verification.
Testing across nine open-weight model pairs (0.5B to 14B parameters) showed that improved audit signal responsiveness reduces baseline audit rates by 2.6x at a 0.95 discount factor.
The new mechanism cuts deviation profits by 31% to 54% while preserving low-latency economic verification.
summary.why_it_matters: It fixes a critical game-theoretic vulnerability in deployed restaking protocols, ensuring long-term cryptographic-free economic security for verifiable LLM inference.
